title: Synthetic crack generation using dynamic programming and elastic deformation to enhance segmentation of concrete and pavement defects
mechanism: Min/max cumulative-energy paths on random noise fields give 1 px crack strands. Variable-width dilation plus geometric and elastic deformation adds width, tortuosity and boundary irregularity.
evidence: 2.25M synthetic samples. Elastic deformation raised feature diversity from 0.17 to 0.31. Trained on synthetic data only: F1 up to 0.79 and mIoU above 0.80 on Cracks-200, CDLN and DeepCrack, comparable to human-annotated training (filter-based segmenter).
adaptation: Deform the skeleton first, then rasterise the label at each source's measured width (ARTS 1.5, CFVS/CSIR 1.75, BMRK 3.0, SDLE 3.25 px). Render a dark profile of about 4 px FWHM with per-source contrast, including the 7% of cracks under 2% contrast. Paste onto labelled cells with full labels, and onto pool multi half-cut cells with loss on the strand and ring only, for E1. Labels are exact, with no jitter.
min_experiment: PF+procedural strands vs PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and recall@2 (half-cut scuff subset reported), test crack IoU as a guard, recall on low-contrast cracks. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.02 or test crack IoU drops by more than 0.012.
prior_overlap: none. Procedural crack synthesis has not been run. Similar to the FreeCOS arm in D06.
